---
title: "Share a passage"
---

Select any sentence on this page and a small toolbar appears above it. You can copy the
plain text, copy it as a Markdown quote ready to paste into your notes, copy a share
link that points a reader straight at the exact words you picked, or cite the passage as a
BibTeX entry that deep-links to it, ready to drop into a reference manager or a `.bib` file.

## A link to the words, not just the page

The share link carries a text fragment, so opening it scrolls the reader to the selected
passage and the browser flashes it into view. The author writes nothing extra: any run of
text becomes its own addressable anchor, because the link encodes the words themselves.

This is the part a static page cannot usually do. A heading anchor takes you to a section;
a text fragment takes you to a phrase. For a dense technical document, being able to hand
someone the single sentence that matters, by link, is the difference between "read this
page" and "read this line".

## Quoting keeps the source

Copy as a quote and you get the passage as a blockquote followed by the document's title and
a link back, so a quotation never loses where it came from. Nothing leaves the page to a
server: the toolbar reads your selection and writes to your clipboard, and the document
itself stays read-only and authoritative.

A second paragraph gives you another place to try it. The longer the passage you select, the
more the link leans on a compact start-and-end form so the URL stays short while still
resolving to the whole run of text you chose.
